info.title: Titan API Document
info.description: ## Introduction All API requests must be over https. All API request/response bodies are formatted as JSON. ## API Endpoints ### US Region - API Base URL: https://bll.titan.email - Control Panel URL: https://manage.titan.email ### EU Region - API Base URL: https://api-euc1.titan.email/bll - Control Panel URL: https://manage-euc1.titan.email ## Authorization between Partner and Titan - To Authorize API requests, an **Authorization** header described below must be added to all requests. - We will share an API Key, which must be added to the **Authorization** header for us to identify the source of the request. - This API Key is a shared secret key between Partner and Titan. - Generally, for any API calls we make to your servers **you must validate** that the same contains this Authorization header and a valid API Key. - Partners should whitelist following Titan IPs - 3.92.40.244, 34.197.244.225, 52.7.187.26 & 3.64.226.220 - It is recommended that partners should provide IPs of their servers to Titan so that Titan can do IP whitelisting for APIs present in this doc. ### Sample Header ``` POST https://bll.titan.email/ HTTP/1.1 Authorization: API.Key API.Key will be provided by us during onboarding Example: Assume we share an **API.Key** with you: 123456abcdefgh- Appropriate Header syntax - POST https://bll.titan.email/partner/createMailOrder HTTP/1.1 Authorization: 123456abcdefgh- ``` ## Error Response - Sample Error Response ```json { "desc":"No Active domain found", "error":"DomainNotFound", "statusCode":404, "reqID":"4605e6ef-ea50-4a81-83f6-06159a9a906b" } ``` - `error` - In case of an error, the server will send a well-defined error response as given below. The API consumers can take a decision regarding the message to be shown based on the error. - e.g : `PartnerNotFound`, `DomainNotFound`, `UserNotFound`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `EXTERNAL_ERROR` etc. - `PartnerNotFound` - Partner does not exist (or is marked inactive) in titan infra. - `UserNotFound` - Customer does not exist in titan infra. - `DomainNotFound` - Domain does not exist (or is marked inactive, in certain cases) in titan infra. - `AccountNotFound` - Email account does not exist (or is marked inactive, in certain cases) in titan infra. - `FORBIDDEN` - Unauthorized Access: Non-Whitelisted Ip - `UNAUTHENTICATED` - No auth header found - If we have messed up, you may get an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`. In such cases, please forward api call details to your Titan PoC. - `statusCode` is standard Http Error Codes. e.g : 404, 401, 500 etc. - `desc` is verbose error description. - Every api in the doc there is a section for possible error codes. ## DNS Records to be added to provision order on Titan - `` mx1.titan.email | mx2.titan.email - `` TXT v=spf1 include:spf.titan.email ~all - _dmarc.`` TXT v=DMARC1;p=none;sp=none;adkim=r;aspf=r;pct=100 (Optional) ## Recommended API Retry logic: Exponential Back off - In case of an HTTP 5XX or a timeout please retry the API call - For each retry wait for 2X the number of seconds of the previous retry until you get an HTTP 200 OK - For e.g. retry after 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s, 64s ... and so on - You may stop retrying after 24 hours and log the same on your side - Parties must notify one another if we continue to get an error or a timeout for greater than 1 hour ## APIs exposed by Titan All APIs, unless specified, are idempotent, hence they can safely be called multiple times. Below URLs are to be used in the request headers to call the APIs in the staging or production environments

tags.name: Redirection between Partner and Titan
tags.description:
All Redirection between Partner website to Titanmail control panel and from Titanmail control panel to Partner website will contain JWT signature for authentication and authorization of data exchanged.
Note - For further information on JSON Web Tokens (JWT) - [Click here](https://jwt.io/introduction/)

Titan mail will provide you one shared API Key which will be used for all API authentication and Hash  computation.
```
    Header
    {
    "typ": "JWT",
    "alg": "HS256"
    }
```

Currently Titanmail supports only the HS256 algorithm.

Construct JWT_TOKEN using the above header and payload specific to each redirect request.

### Autologin Titan user into webmail

To auto login the Titan user into [webmail](https://app.titan.email/), redirect to Titan webmail with these query params:
- webmailAutoLoginToken as **slt** (You will receive this token in the response whenever you create an email account)
- created email as **email_account**
- true as **clearSession** (This is optional. Add parameter in case the expectation is to log out any existing logged in accounts on [webmail](https://app.titan.email/))

Example: https://app.titan.email/?slt=1:nkLjBJX9Uqgy&email_account=james@xyz.com

Note: webmailAutoLoginToken is a short lived token which is meant to be used immediately in the flow after creating an email account. This token should not be persisted and can't be used later to auto login into [webmail](https://app.titan.email/).

tags.name: Titan Event Notification
tags.description:
These are the webhooks configured for event notification between from the Titan cloud infrastructure to the partner.

There will be webhooks provided to the Partner for notifications of changes occurring on Titan’s end.
All event notification calls will be made until a confirmation of success is received (HTTP 200). In case of failure, we will reattempt to push a notification once every minute until we receive a confirmation of success. A unique event ID will be passed against each event as a unique identifier in order to prevent duplication. In order to ensure that the events are passed securely, the following measures will be put in place -
* The Partner Key will be sent in the **Authorization** header of all the requests.
* Source IPs will be shared with the Partner during deployment

**Note** - The following IPs will need to be whitelisted by the partner - 3.92.40.244, 34.197.244.225, 52.7.187.26 & 3.64.226.220.

Titan will notify partners on various life cycle events of a Mail Order or an Email Account.

### On Mail Order creation at Titan

**Note**:

- noOfAccounts represents the total number of accounts a user has purchased.
- customerName, customerEmailAddress, customerCountry, billingCycle are optional fields

``` json

    {
        "id": "<unique event id>",
        "event": "MAIL_ORDER_CREATED",
        "data":{
            "titanOrderId": "<Titan Mail generated unique ID>",
            "domainName": "domain name",
            "customerId": "Unique customer Id on your side for this customer",
            "customerName": "customer name",
            "customerEmailAddress": "customer email address",
            "customerCountry": "< 2 letter ISO CODE, e.g. US>",
            "planType": "<plan-name>",
            "expiryDate": "<utc-expiry-date.format-yyyy-MM-dd>",
            "storageLimit": "<integer-limit-in-mb>",
            "noOfAccounts": "<integer-number-of-accounts-in-plan>",
            "billingCycle": "monthly",
            "status": "active|pending",
            "metadata": {
              "cpanelHostName": "<cPanel hostname where this hosting order provisioned>",
              "cpanelUserName": "<cPanel username associated with this account>"
            }
        }
    }
```

### On Mail Order status update at Titan

**Note** :

- type - type of the suspension like abuse, expiry, employee left
- If a domain is suspended with some suspension type then it can only be unblocked by that type only.
- suspenderRole - The entity that suspended the email account. It can have following values
    - titan
    - titanSupport
    - partner
    - partnerSupport
    - domainAdmin - The email account admin that is part of only this domain
    - accountAdmin - The Person that get the domain provisioned in the Titan
    - account - the email account holder person
- suspenderRole have precedence in following order
  - (titan , titanSupport) > (partner, partnerSupport) > (domainAdmin, accountAdmin) > account
- The higher precedence member can remove the lower precedence member suspension
- suspendedOn - suspension date in YYYY-MM-DD format

``` json
    {
        "id": "<unique event id>",
        "event": "MAIL_ORDER_STATUS_UPDATED",
        "data": {
          "titanOrderId": "<Titan Mail generated unique ID>",
          "domainName": "domain name",
          "customerId": "Unique customer Id on your side for this customer",
          "oldStatus": "active | pending | suspended | deleted",
          "newStatus": "active | suspended | deleted",
          "suspensions": [
            {
                "type": "abuse",
                "suspenderRole": "titanSupport",
                "suspendedOn": "2021-01-13"
            }
          ]
        }
    }
```

**Note** :

### Titan Control Panel iframe events

To consume the events posted to the container website via [window.postMessage()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage) from the embedded Titan Control Panel.

#### Message structure in titan control panel

- Parameters Description:
  - event (string, required)
  - data (object, optional)
- Sample format:
  ``` json
  {
    "event": "<EVENT_NAME>",
    "data": "<DATA_TO_BE_SENT>"
  }
  ```

#### Events Handling in partner panel

Use [addEventListener()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener) method to set up a function to be called whenever a message is posted from the iframe to the partner panel.
``` js
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
    if(event.data.event) {
      //Do needful action here//
    }
}, false);
```

#### Events list

These are the standard events sent from Iframe Titan control panel to partner panel.

**PAGE_DID_LOAD**

- Usage

  Container websites can show some view or take some action based on the page currently loaded in the iframe. For eg. By listening to the content of the page, you can save events of which pages within the Titan CP your customers visit. Or you could choose to show a dynamic FAQ section that has FAQ's relevant to the page the user is on.

- Trigger

  Event posted whenever a page is displayed to the user. All pages have been set up to communicate with the parent window via postMessage API.

- Example:
  ``` json
  {
    "event": "PAGE_DID_LOAD",
    "data": {
        "pageName": "<PAGE_NAME>" /* Current path name */
    }
  }
  ```

**PAYMENT_ACTION**

- Usage

  Container websites may choose to redirect the user to the payment URLs in the same tab instead of default behaviour of opening new tabs with payment URLs.

- Trigger

  Event posted whenever a user takes action related to payments eg: upgrading plan, buying more accounts, renew etc.

- Example:
  ``` json
  {
    "event": "PAYMENT_ACTION",
    "data": {
       "action":"upgradePlan|buyMoreAccounts|renewOrder|billing",
       "titanOrderId": "<Titan Mail generated unique ID>",
       "domainName": "example.com",
       "customerId": "<customerID>",
       "planType": "free|pro|premium",
       "noOfAccounts": "<Total no of current accounts>",
       "expiryDate": "<utc-expiry-date.format-yyyy-MM-dd>"
    }
  }
  ```

- Parameters Description

  | Parameters | Description | Purpose of the parameter | Data Type |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | action | Relevant action taken by the customer | This is used to signal the relevant billing option selected by the customer in the Titan control panel. Accordingly, billing and upgrade options should be shown to customers on the partner payment page | Enum |
  | titanOrderId | The unique Titan order ID against which the domain is provisioned | The titanOrderId is used to identify the order being referenced | Enum |
  | domainName | Customer Domain being provisioned | The order provisioned in Titanmail is against the domainName provided by the partner within the API | Alphanumeric - upto 64 characters |
  | customerId | The customer ID stored on your end for each customer | This is used to identify all the orders linked to a particular customer | Alphanumeric - upto 64 characters |
  | planType | Current Titan plan type configured for the customer | This is used to identify the existing Titan plan for the customer and show relevant upgrade options to the customer on Partner end | Enum |
  | noOfAccounts | The current number of accounts or mailboxes configured for the customer | This can be used by Partner to identify the current number of email accounts for the customer and allow the customer to upgrade the accounts accordingly | Integer |
  | expiryDate | Date on which the existing package is set to expire | We assign the expiry date in our systems based on this parameter | YYYY-MM-DD |

**CONTENT_DIMENSION_DID_UPDATE**

- Usage

  Container websites may show content outside iframe and adjust iframe dimensions to align iframe and other views properly. For eg. To render some content just below the iframe, within the container website control panel. (an FAQ box, an NPS survey, a promotion banner etc)

- Trigger

  Event posted whenever the control panel content's height or width is updated by new content.

- Example:
  ``` json
  {
      "event": "CONTENT_DIMENSION_DID_UPDATE",
      "data": {
          "height": <val>,
          "width": <val>,
      }
  }
  ```

- Parameters Description:
  - height : maximum height of current content inside control panel
  - width: current width of control panel iframe

- Note

  However if the user changes the control panel dimension from **outside interaction**, such as dragging the width of the iframe to increase / decrease (if any such option is given by partners), then the partner panel window, first need to send postMessage Info to iframe with the below sample format:

  Sample format:
  ``` js
  // Trigger when iframe's width is changed by user externally //
  iframeElement.contentWindow.postMessage({
      event: "IFRAME_WIDTH_DID_UPDATE",
      iframeWindowWidth: 80 + "vw" // Sample width after change
      }, '*');
      iframeElement.style.width =
      new_iframe_width // set new iframe width here
  })
  ```

  After listening to the IFRAME_WIDTH_DID_UPDATE event, the iframe window will trigger the event CONTENT_DIMENSION_DID_UPDATE with the format specified above.

**LOADER_DID_APPEAR**

- Usage

  Container websites may choose to hide content outside the iframe while the iframe page loads. For eg. the FAQ box outside the iframe can be hidden while the user is navigating between pages within the iframe.

- Trigger

  Event posted whenever new content fetching in the control panel is in progress, a loader is shown. If the partner panel wants to listen/show some UI only when the iframe is fully loaded, they can use this event to disable the interactions till the page is loaded. Partner can rely on other events 'PAGE_DID_LOAD' or 'CONTENT_DIMENSION_DID_UPDATE' to take action when the loader is hidden.

- Example:
  ``` js
  window.addEventListener("message", (event) =>
      {
          const eventName = event.data.event;
          if (eventName === LOADER_DID_APPEAR) {
          //here partner panel can decide to hide some sections until iframe is fully loaded e.g not showing FAQ section
      })
  ```

**EMAIL_ACCOUNTS_CHANGED**

- Usage

  The container websites might need to dynamically update the number of purchased/active email accounts. They can do so by adding a listener to this event.

  Format of the event:
  ```json
  {
      "event": "EMAIL_ACCOUNTS_CHANGED",
      "data": {
          "active": <val>,
          "purchased": <val>,
          "limit": <val>
      }
  }
  ```

  Example Usage:
  ```javascript
  window.addEventListener('message', function(event) {
      const eventData = event.data;
      const eventName = eventData.event;
      if (eventName === "EMAIL_ACCOUNTS_CHANGED") {
          const mailboxData = eventData.data;
          console.log("The number of active email accounts in use are: ", mailboxData.active);
          console.log("The number of total purchased email accounts are: ", mailboxData.purchased);
          console.log("The number of limit to email accounts are: ", mailboxData.limit);
      }
  });
  ```

- Trigger

  Whenever there is a change in the number of purchased/active mailboxes, we make an API call from our Frontend. If we detect any changes in the number of accounts, active or purchased, we will send this event as a postMessage.

post.description:
API to provision a Mail Order on Titan.

**Notes** :
- Control Panel password details will be sent via email to customerEmailAddress. If you need to disable it, please contact titan support.
- We don't support IDN domains.

domainName.description:
Customer mail order being provisioned
The order provisioned in Titanmail is against the domainName provided by the partner within the API

orderId.description: The order ID stored on your end for this mail order, if any. If needed, You can use this data to correlate orders at your end and in Titan.The data is returned in [listMailOrders](#operation/listMailOrders) call.

customerId.description:
The customer ID stored on your end for each customer
This is used to identify all the orders linked to a particular customer

customerName.description: Name of the customer as stored in the partner's system. It is recommended to send the full name as we utilize this for any communication sent across to the customer.

customerEmailAddress.description:
The email address with which the customer registers on the partner website
This email is used in order for us to send out the password setup email or any signup/usage nudges to get the customer to utilize the email
This email will be used by the customer to login into [Control Panel](https://manage.titan.email). This user will also be the primary admin for the domain

alternateEmailAddress.description: This email will be used to send emails, in case email delivery fails for customerEmailAddress

password.description: Password for signing into Domain [Control Panel](https://manage.titan.email)

customerCountry.description:
Should be the 2 letter ISO Code, country from which the customer is accessing partner website/making the purchase.
We will use this to identify the localized pricing based on the location of the customer in cases where Titan mail is managing the billing.

planType.description: This is the Titan mail plan to be provisioned for the provided mail order. This would vary based on the plans being positioned with the partner. It is highly recommended to provide payment details in case this is a paid plan

noOfAccounts.description:
Required for Paid Plans
The number of accounts or mailboxes to be provisioned against the domain.
This is used as a limiting parameter for the user to create accounts within the [Control Panel](https://manage.titan.email). E.g. if this is set to 2, the user will not be allowed to create more than 2 mailboxes

titanResellerId.description:
Titan Reseller ID for reseller-level branding. If provided, the order will use the branding associated with this reseller.

get.description:
API to check a mail order with given domainName is available for provisioning on Titan

**Availability behaviour**

- **`isAvailable: true`** — the domain is available for the requesting partner to create a mail order.
- **`isAvailable: false`** — the requesting partner already has an order for this domain; its details are returned in the response (`titanOrderId`, `customerDetails`, `orderDetails`).
- The same domain can have a mail order under multiple partners, but only one of those orders is serviceable at a time; the others are non-serviceable. Even when the domain is already serviceable under a different partner, this API returns `true` and the partner can still create an order — it is created in a **non-serviceable** state.
    - **Serviceable** — all email services are allowed.
    - **Non-serviceable** — email services are not allowed, but the user can still log in to their account.
- To make the order serviceable, the user must prove ownership of the domain. Once ownership is verified, an automated status-switch job makes the order serviceable and moves the previously serviceable order to non-serviceable — no manual action is required.
- _We are updating our mail interfaces to guide users on how to prove domain ownership, making this state easier to understand._

get.description:
When the user selects to upgrade or buy more email accounts we will redirect the user to your payment page to complete the purchase process and do the payment.
`<partner-payment-url>/upgrade?jwt=<JWT_TOKEN>`

`<partner-payment-url>` is configurable, also can be decorated with `domain_name`, `order_id`, `locale`.

e.g : `<payment-url>/{domain_name}`

#### Parameters
+ jwt (string, required)
    + Jwt Request Body
        ``` json
            {
            "titanOrderId": 21312,
            "domainName": "domain.name",
            "customerId": "anson123",
            "planType": "premium",
            "noOfAccounts": 10,
            "expiryDate": "2021-05-21",
            "action":"upgradePlan",
            "trackingId": "tracking-id",
            "currency": "USD",
            "chargeAmount": 3.14
            }
        ```

    + titanOrderId (number, required)
        + The unique Titan order ID against which the domain is provisioned
    + domainName (string, required)
        + Customer Domain being provisioned
    + customerId (string, required)
        + The customer ID stored on your end for each customer
    + planType (string, required)
        + Current Titan plan type configured for the customer
    + noOfAccounts (number, required)
        + The current number of accounts or mailboxes configured for the customer
    + expiryDate (string, required)
        + Date on which the package is set to expire in YYYY-MM-DD
    + action (string, required)
        + Relevant action taken by the customer
            + upgradePlan
            + buyMoreAccounts
            + renewOrder
            + billing

        + This is used to signal the relevant billing option selected by the customer in the Titan control panel. Accordingly, billing and upgrade options should be shown to customers on the partner payment page
    + trackingId (string, optional)

    + currency (string, optional)
        + This is currency used for calculations.
        + Experimental, see [Complete Purchase API](#operation/completePurchase). Discuss with Titan team before using it.
    + chargeAmount (number, optional)
        + This is amount to be charged.
        + Experimental, see [Complete Purchase API](#operation/completePurchase). Discuss with Titan team before using it.

post.description:
Notification APIs should be used post discussion. This is a reference document as to how notifications can be used by a
partner. This can be decided upon if there is utility for these notifications

* **Note** :
    + HOSTING_PURCHASED
        + This Event notifies Titan that a hosting plan has been purchased at partner's end and the user is eligible for
          a Titan plan. This information helps in tracking the signup (attach) rates.
    + REFUND_ISSUED
        + This Event notifies Titan that a refund has been issued from partner to the customer.
        + Event can be called for active/suspended/deleted mail order.
        + If API is called multiple times with same `paymentTxnId` and different data (domainName,
          refundAmount refundTaxAmount, refundUSDAmount and currency), partner will get `BAD_REQUEST` exception else no
          action is taken.
    + MAIL_ORDER_SETUP_COMPLETED
        + On this API notification we will mark order's setup as completed and stop showing relevant upgrade/purchase
          hooks
    + MAIL_ORDER_PURCHASED
        + This Event notifies Titan that mail order is purchased and contains details related to transaction.
        + This Event is only used for reference and reporting on our end.
    + PAYMENT_DATA_BULK
        + This Event notifies Titan of the customer's purchase of standalone email order / additional mailbox purchases
          / Titan order upgrades / Titan order renewals.
        + Max batch size of the event is 100 orders
    + REFUND_ISSUED_BULK
        + This Event notifies Titan that a refund has been issued from partner to the customer in bulk.
        + Max batch size of the event is 100 orders.
    + CREDIT_ISSUED
        + This Event notifies Titan that a credit has been issued from partner to the customer.
    + MAIL_ORDER_PURCHASE_CANCELED
        + This Event notifies Titan that mail order is canceled.
        + Send this event when user has purchased standalone email plan, does not setup the email during plan duration
          and doesn't renew on plan expiry.
    + MODIFY_MAIL_ORDER_DETAILS
        + This Event notifies Titan that mail order details has been modified.

get.description: API to check if deleted Email Account can be reactivated.

parameters.name: titanOrderId
parameters.description: The unique Titan order Id

parameters.name: titanAccountId
parameters.description: The unique Titan account Id

purgeAt.description:
In `yyyy-MM-dd` format. All the account data would be purged from our system permanently on this date.
Account is expected to be in the deleted state and not already purged. Domain should be active state.
It should be greater than or equal to today's date. Present when reactivationAllowed is true and purgeAt is set or
reactivationAllowed is not allowed due to account is purged.

reason.description: This is an enum with values. This field will be present if reactivationAllowed is false - `DOMAIN_INACTIVE`: The mail order (domain) this account belongs to is not active or suspended - `ANOTHER_ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS`: Another account already exists with the same email address - `ACCOUNT_NOT_IN_DELETED_STATE`: The account is not in a deleted state - `ACCOUNT_PURGED`: The account's purge date has passed and it can no longer be recovered
